best_for: Students and hobbyists learning C or C++ on Windows who want a free IDE with a compiler in the same download and no project files to hand-write.
description:
Code::Blocks is an IDE for C, C++ and Fortran from the Code::Blocks Team. It is written in C++ on the wxWidgets toolkit and built around plugins: even compiling and debugging come from plugins, and you can add almost any feature by installing or writing one.

Builds can run in parallel on your CPU's extra cores, and a workspace can hold several projects that depend on each other, each with multiple targets. The editor has code completion, a class browser, code folding, smart indent and a one-key swap between a header and its source file. A to-do list can track tasks for different people. You can also set breakpoints that stop only when a condition is true or after a set number of hits.

points.title: Get the MinGW build if unsure
points.text: The project recommends the Windows setup that bundles GCC, G++, GFortran, Clang and GDB from WinLibs (version 14.2.0). The plain installer has no compiler, so you would need to add one.

points.title: No admin rights needed
points.text: Besides the normal installer there is a non-admin installer and a zip that needs no setup, in 64-bit and 32-bit builds. This site lists x86 and x64 installers for the current user or the whole machine, and the zips.

points.title: Works with many compilers
points.text: It drives GCC, MSVC, Clang, Open Watcom and others through its own build system, so you do not write makefiles. It can also import Visual Studio and Dev-C++ projects.

points.title: Debugging through GDB
points.text: The debugger front end uses GDB, with breakpoints, watches, call stack, memory and register views. Support for Microsoft's CDB is limited.

points.title: Free and GPL licensed
points.text: Code::Blocks is open source under GPLv3, with no paid edition.

points.title: Slow release pace
points.text: Releases are years apart: the Windows listing here keeps only 2 versions, ending at 25.03. Linux lists only the current Flatpak, a community build for x64 and Arm64 that Flathub does not mark as verified.

points.title: Mac is shaky
points.text: The project offers a macOS 25.03 build but says it is unstable for lack of Mac developers. This site does not list it.
